CVE-2026-102894.title: GPUStack: SAML callback trusts an unverified SAMLResponse, allowing authentication bypass and account takeover
CVE-2026-102894.description: GPUStack is an open-source GPU cluster manager for AI model serving and GPU instance provisioning. From 0.7.1 until 2.2.2, the /auth/saml/callback endpoint decoded SAML XML, used its NameID and attributes to resolve or provision a user, and minted a gpustack_session JWT without calling OneLogin_Saml2_Auth.process_response to verify the signature, issuer, audience, destination, or time conditions. CVE-2026-113782.description: ESP-IDF is the Espressif Internet of Things (IOT) Development Framework. From 5.2.0 until 5.2.8, 5.3.6, 5.4.5, 5.5.5, and 6.0.3, the OpenThread Border Router Neighbor Discovery packet handler trusts an attacker-controlled ICMPv6 option length while copying into a fixed stack buffer. Exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction and can crash or reboot the device or corrupt adjacent stack state. Prior to 0.12.30, the generic GET /api/{entity} list endpoint accepts attacker-controlled sort values in PaginatedFindAllWithoutFilters in server/resource/resource_findallpaginated.go without validating the requested column against the table schema. The code uses those values for SELECT and ORDER BY identifier construction, so an embedded identifier quote can terminate the quoted identifier and make the remainder parse as SQL, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to extract unauthorized table data through blind or error-based behavior or repeatedly trigger query failures. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.30.

CVE-2026-97174.title: Keycloak-services: keycloak-services: ciba sub parameter injection causes attacker authentication to issue victim tokens
CVE-2026-97174.description: A flaw was found in the Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication (CIBA) implementation of Keycloak. The CIBA endpoint fails to properly validate the sub parameter, allowing it to be stored as an additional request parameter. During the token issuance process, this injected value overwrites the legitimate subject identifier. This allows an attacker to authenticate as themselves but receive security tokens belonging to a different victim user, leading to unauthorized account access.

CVE-2026-99468.title: media: imx-jpeg: cancel timeout worker when streaming stops
CVE-2026-99468.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: imx-jpeg: cancel timeout worker when streaming stops

Each per-fd context ctx owns a delayed_work (ctx->task_timer, callback
mxc_jpeg_device_run_timeout) armed via schedule_delayed_work() at the end
of mxc_jpeg_device_run() to recover a stalled encode/decode job. The only
existing cancellation is cancel_delayed_work() in the frame-done IRQ
handler, which de-queues a pending work item but does not wait for a
callback that has already started, and it only runs when a frame completes.

When the fd is closed while a job is in flight (the frame-done IRQ has not
fired yet), nothing syncs the worker before mxc_jpeg_release() frees ctx
with kfree() after v4l2_m2m_ctx_release(). A queued or executing
mxc_jpeg_device_run_timeout() can then recover ctx through
container_of(&ctx->task_timer) and dereference it (ctx->mxc_jpeg,
slot_data, dev_warn) after ctx has been freed.

CVE-2026-99486.title: rust: configfs: fix data offset calculation for subsystem callbacks
CVE-2026-99486.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

rust: configfs: fix data offset calculation for subsystem callbacks

`get_group_data()` chooses between `Group::<Parent>::container_of()` and
`Subsystem::<Parent>::container_of()` based on whether `this` represents
the root group of a configfs subsystem. It detects this by checking
`(*this).cg_subsys.is_null()`, but `link_group()` in `fs/configfs/dir.c`
unconditionally sets `cg_subsys` for every `config_group` attached anywhere
in a registered subsystem, including the subsystem's own `su_group`. The
only `config_group` with a NULL `cg_subsys` is the configfs root, on which
userspace cannot trigger callbacks. The check is therefore always false at
runtime, and the `Subsystem` branch is dead. Subsystem-level callbacks
reach the `Group` branch and may read `data` at the wrong offset.

Thus change the `is_root` check to correctly identify whether a group is a
root group by comparing `this` to `subsys.su_group`.
